summary: The candidate is correct as a conditional theorem. Applying (H2) to the complete lattice epigraph approximation gives the correctly normalized cubic mass factor. The uniform halfspace and depth bounds, vertical Lipschitz estimate, endpoint-inclusive Riemann bound, and tail estimate justify both squared-moment limits. The unconditional separation argument preserves the original source weights and yields the factor 5, hence the stated logarithmic hitting constant. The accepted same-table root comparison and attained actual-body depth bound give the claimed point with the required quantifier order. The uniform parity argument and the one-dimensional quantile argument establish both unconditional calibrations. One-point and lower-rank supports, zero mixed volume, atoms, endpoint masses, and cutoff equalities are covered. No first-moment hypothesis is used; (H2) remains an explicit unproved premise.
